newsitem.title: SPAIN: Alcoa to buy Spain's Inespal for 61.5 bln ptas.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa to buy Spain's Inespal for 61.5 bln ptas.

text.p: Spanish holding group SEPI said on Tuesday it had signed an agreement to sell aluminium group Inespal to U.S.-based Aluminum Company of America (Alcoa) for 61.5 billion pesetas.
In addition, Alcoa will invest 65 billion pesetas in the group, SEPI said in a statement.

The operation "includes among its conditions the development of Alcoa's industrial programme, whose principal projects are plans for investment of 65 billion pesetas, the global maintenance of the workforce and the increase of group activity," the statement said.
The operation affects Inespal's four main business divisions and a total of nine industrial plants and central services in Madrid.
Inespal workers had initially protested against a deal, which had been provisionally agreed in February, with a series of short strikes amid job loss fears. They called off strikes last week.
"SEPI considers that the Alcoa offer supposes a guarantee of viability for the Inespal industrial project," the statement said.
Since 1990, given volatility in the aluminium business, has accumulated losses of more than 67 billion pesetas despite turning a profit in the last two years.

Inespal will represent 50 percent of Alcoa's European revenue. It will represent 100 percent of Alcoa's European aluminium production, 67 percent of its primary aluminium and 52 percent of its laminates.
The deal includes all but two of Inespal's units. Ferroperfil is set for a management buyout while Inespal Conversion, housed in Linares, will remain in the public group.
The two groups did not fit into Alcoa's strategic plan, said SEPI, which will guarantee the viability of the Linares plant.

In a news conference, Industry Minister Josep Pique said: "A key part of the deal is the industrial plan which I consider very appropriate from both the labour side, as it ensures jobs as well as more investments than Inespal had planned."
In addition to Inespal, Spain resolved the future of steel-producer CSI on Tuesday, agreeing to sell a 35 percent stake to Luxembourg steel maker Arbed.
Pique said the process of aggressive privatisation would continue.
"Now the process has picked up pace. We're are going to continue down this road because I think its what this country needs and it has been well-received by the markets," Pique said.
